CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

The appeal is filed by the claimants -appellants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.316/2011 dated 30.01.2012 by the Addl.

Senior Civil Judge & Motor Accident Claim Tribunal-14,
at Bhadravathi seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that on 07.12.2010 at about 8.45 p.m. while K.M. Gurushanthappa -deceased was proceeding towards Machenahalli by riding his Motor bike bearing No.KA-01/S-6522 on B.H. Road, near old Jedikatte, Bhadravathi, a Tiller bearing Reg.No.KA-13-4/T-7177/78 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against deceased motorcycle from backside, due Smt Mahalakshmi vs Nagaraja on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189850221/
2 to which, deceased fell on the ground, sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Therefore, the claimants have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
The accident, death of the deceased and liability to pay the compensation are not in dispute.
The deceased who was aged 56 years old died in the motor vehicle accident.
The accident had caused on 07.12.2010.
The deceased was a head constable serving in the Karnataka State Reserve Police.
It is found that the Tribunal has awarded lesser compensation.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as per law.

Ex-P8 is the certificate which proves NC:
2024:KHC:45651 that the deceased was drawing a salary of Rs.20,003/-.
Accordingly, his monthly salary is taken at Rs.20,000/-.
The deceased was 56 years old.
Therefore, 15% income is added towards 'loss of future income in life'.
If the deceased was alive, then he would have got promotion during his service.
Accordingly, 15% of income is added towards 'loss of future prospects in life'.
The appropriate multiplier is '9'.
There are three dependants to the deceased.
Hence, 1/3rd of income is deducted towards 'personal expenses' of the deceased.
Therefore, the 'loss of dependency' is re-
assessed and quantified as under:
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.16,56,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' as against Rs.1,15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

6. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'loss of consortium'
which is a meager amount and the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head 'Loss of love and affection'.
The loss of love and affection NC: 2024:KHC:45651 and loss of consortium are having the same connotation.
As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others1, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- with 10% escalation.

sentences.text: Hence, in the present case, there are three dependants.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3 dependants + 10% escalation) is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium including loss of love and affection'.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'loss of estate'.

Hence, a compensation of Rs.16,500/-(Rs.15,000/- +10% escalation) is awarded under the head 'loss of estate'.
8.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head 'funeral expenses'.

Hence, a compensation of Rs.16,500/-(Rs.15,000/- +10% escalation) is awarded under the head 'transportation of dead body and 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2024:KHC:45651 funeral expenses' as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
